title: FA Cup fourth round: League One Mansfield beat Burnley to increase pressure on Scott Parker
content:
League One Mansfield Town pulled off a giant-killing in Saturday’s FA Cup fourth round with a 2-1 win over top flight strugglers Burnley.

A late goal from Louis Reed completed Mansfield’s comeback from a goal down at Turf Moor to increase the pressure on Burnley boss Scott Parker.

The Premier League side took a 21st-minute lead through Josh Laurent but Mansfield – who are 13th in League One, English football’s third tier, and coached by Nigel Clough, son of the late Brian Clough – levelled after the break through Rhys Oates.

Reed curled home a brilliant 25-yard free kick to book Mansfield’s place in round five for the first time since 1975 and leave Parker’s position feeling more precarious as 19th-placed Burnley slide towards an immediate return to the Championship.

Earlier on Saturday, Burton Albion, also of League One, nearly pulled off an even bigger shock after taking West Ham United to extra-time following a goalless draw after 90 minutes.

Crysencio Summerville’s 95th minute goal spared the blushes of Nuno Espirito Santo’s visiting side, who were reduced to ten men minutes later when midfielder Freddie Potts was shown a straight red card.

Manchester City navigated a potential banana skin of their own on Saturday, beating League Two outfit Salford Town 2-0 at the Etihad Stadium thanks to an own goal by Tottenham Hotspur’s on-loan defender Alfie Dorrington and Marc Guehi’s first goal for the club.

National League Macclesfield Town will be aiming to pull off another spectacular upset on Monday night when they host top flight Brentford, having recorded statistically the biggest upset in the FA Cup’s storied history by eliminating Crystal Palace in the third round.

Norwich City beat West Bromwich Albion 3-1 to progress, while in Saturday’s other all-Championship tie, Oliver Skipp’s acrobatic effort ensure that Leicester City took Southampton to extra-time at St Mary’s Stadium.

On Friday, Chelsea beat Hull City 4-0 and Wrexham edged past Ipswich Town 1-0 to reach the fifth-round for the first time since 1997.
